I need to build a knowledge base from recent papers about large language model fine-tuning and alignment. Please access our academic paper repository and read the full content of papers that are relevant to the topics of LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements. For each relevant paper, read through its sections carefully to understand the methodology and key results. Skip any papers that are about unrelated topics like robotics or physical systems.

Create a Notion page titled LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base. The page should contain blocks for each relevant paper, where each block covers the paper title, the key method introduced, and the main findings from the paper.

Also create a Word document called LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx in my workspace. The document should start with a heading called LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey, followed by an introduction paragraph. Then include a dedicated section for each relevant paper that presents the paper title, the author names, a description of the method, and the key results extracted from reading the paper sections.

Finally, create a Google Sheet called LLM Paper Registry with columns for ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Key_Contribution, and Method_Category, with one row per relevant paper.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself runs the compact discovery queries, then uses one parallel full-text reader wave of three per-paper explorers and one parallel writer wave of three deliverable owners.

Before Wave 1, the main agent covers the task-relevant local arXiv candidate space in read-only mode through complementary fine-tuning, alignment, and architecture queries at the supported per-call bound; unions and deduplicates all returned IDs (the search exposes no cursor); applies the task's relevance rule (reject robotics or physical-system distractors); and freezes exactly three retained paper IDs — never importing outside facts or importing rejected IDs downstream.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per retained paper ID:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Reader for retained paper 1. Use the local repository read_paper tool with paper_id = that literal assigned ID, read through ALL sections of the paper (not just the abstract) to understand the methodology and key results, and return EXACTLY the structured report {paper_id, title, full authors, published date, key method, source-backed findings, method category, section coverage}. Read-only: do not create Notion, Word, Google Sheet, or intermediate files.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Reader for retained paper 2 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Reader for retained paper 3 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies one handoff per retained ID, deduplicates titles, verifies every rejected paper against the exclusion rule, and freezes one normalized packet with per-paper controls.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the single Notion page exclusively. Search for LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base, create at most one page, add one substantive block per frozen paper with title, method, and findings, and read it back. Return page ID/title, paper coverage, block count, and validation. Do not write the Word document or Google Sheet.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx exclusively. Create it exactly once with the required heading, introduction, and one author/method/results section for every frozen paper. Read it back and return path, headings, retained-paper coverage, and validation. Do not modify Notion or Google Sheets.
3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Google Sheet LLM Paper Registry exclusively. Create it once with the exact six columns and one row per frozen paper, preserving full authors and source dates and using controlled Method_Category values. Read it back and return spreadsheet/sheet IDs, headers, row count, and validation. Do not write Notion or Word state.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile the same stable-ID set, authors, methods, and findings across all deliverables, verify every rejected paper appears nowhere, and complete only after file and external-state checks. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

nodes.text:
Access the available academic paper repository. Review every stored paper sufficiently to classify relevance, excluding robotics and physical-systems papers. For each paper relevant to LLM fine-tuning, alignment, or model-architecture improvements, read the full stored content and sections carefully. Return a structured synthesis with: ArXiv ID, exact title, all authors, published date, key method introduced, main findings/results, and a concise method category. Also list excluded papers with a brief exclusion reason so coverage is auditable. Do not create or modify artifacts; this is read-only research. Acceptance: all repository papers considered, every included paper supported by full-content reading, and fields complete enough to populate Notion, Word, and Google Sheets.
Review relevant LLM papers

Create a Notion page titled exactly "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base" in an appropriate accessible workspace parent (use search to identify a suitable existing page; if multiple, choose the most general workspace/home page). Add an introductory paragraph and one clearly separated section/block group per paper below. Each paper must include title, key method introduced, and main findings. Use concise, substantive prose.

Papers:
1) Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv 2305.20050). Method: DPO analytically reformulates RLHF reward maximization as a classification-style objective on preferred/rejected response pairs, optimizing against a frozen reference policy without a separate reward model or on-policy PPO. Findings: matched or exceeded PPO-based RLHF on sentiment control, summarization, and dialogue; comparable/better response quality with simpler, more stable, lighter training.
2) Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models (arXiv 2307.09288). Method: 7B/13B/70B foundation models and Llama 2-Chat; supervised fine-tuning plus iterative RLHF using preference data, reward modeling, rejection-sampling fine-tuning, and PPO; safety data/red-teaming, Ghost Attention, and grouped-query attention in 70B. Findings: improved over LLaMA on benchmarks; chat models generally surpassed evaluated open-source peers and were competitive with major closed systems on helpfulness/safety; safety work reduced unsafe generations, with remaining factuality, reasoning, multilingual, and prompt-sensitivity limits.
3) Mistral 7B (arXiv 2310.06825). Method: decoder-only 7B model combining grouped-query attention and sliding-window attention, with rolling KV cache/chunked prefill; also an instruction-fine-tuned variant. Findings: outperformed Llama 2 13B across reported benchmark groupings and Llama 1 34B on many reasoning/math/code tasks; competitive coding performance and stronger general language; instruct model beat compared 7B instruction models; reduced cache/inference costs.

Do not include the excluded robotics paper. Return the created page ID and URL plus a concise confirmation of its block structure. Acceptance: exact title and all three paper sections with required fields.
Build Notion knowledge base

Create a polished Word document at exactly `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-review-notion-word/workspace/LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx`. It must begin with Heading 1 text exactly `LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey`, followed immediately by an introduction paragraph. Then create a dedicated Heading 2 section for each of the three papers below. Each section must include the exact title, author names, a clear method description, and key results. Include arXiv ID and publication date where useful. Do not include the robotics paper. Ensure readable professional formatting and verify the document by extracting its text/outline after creation.

Source synthesis:
1) ArXiv 2305.20050, `Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model`; authors Rafael Rafailov; Archit Sharma; Eric Mitchell; Stefano Ermon; Christopher D. Manning; Chelsea Finn; published 2023-05-29. Method: DPO analytically reformulates RLHF reward maximization as a binary classification-style loss over preferred/rejected response pairs, directly optimizing the LM relative to a frozen reference policy without separately fitting a reward model or using on-policy PPO. Results: matched or exceeded PPO-based RLHF across sentiment control, summarization, and dialogue; comparable or better generation quality, simpler implementation, better stability, and lower computational overhead.
2) ArXiv 2307.09288, `Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models`; authors Hugo Touvron; Louis Martin; Kevin Stone; Peter Albert; Amjad Almahairi; Yasmine Babaei; Nikolay Bashlykov; Soumya Batra; Prajjwal Bhargava; Shruti Bhosale; Dan Bikel; Lukas Blecher; Cristian Canton Ferrer; Moya Chen; Guillem Cucurull; David Esiobu; Jude Fernandes; Jeremy Fu; Wenyin Fu; Brian Fuller; Cynthia Gao; Vedanuj Goswami; Naman Goyal; Anthony Hartshorn; Saghar Hosseini; Rui Hou; Hakan Inan; Marcin Kardas; Viktor Kerkez; Madian Khabsa; Isabel Kloumann; Artem Korenev; Punit Singh Koura; Marie-Anne Lachaux; Thibaut Lavril; Jenya Lee; Diana Liskovich; Yinghai Lu; Yuning Mao; Xavier Martinet; Todor Mihaylov; Pushkar Mishra; Igor Molybog; Yixin Nie; Andrew Poulton; Jeremy Reizenstein; Rashi Rungta; Kalyan Saladi; Alan Schelten; Ruan Silva; Eric Michael Smith; Ranjan Subramanian; Xiaoqing Ellen Tan; Binh Tang; Ross Taylor; Adina Williams; Jian Xiang Kuan; Puxin Xu; Zheng Yan; Iliyan Zarov; Yuchen Zhang; Angela Fan; Melanie Kambadur; Sharan Narang; Aurelien Rodriguez; Robert Stojnic; Sergey Edunov; Thomas Scialom; published 2023-07-18. Method: 7B, 13B, 70B pretrained family and Llama 2-Chat; SFT then iterative RLHF using preference collection, reward models, rejection-sampling fine-tuning and PPO; safety-specific data, red-teaming, Ghost Attention, and GQA in 70B. Results: gains over original LLaMA on benchmarks; chat models generally better than compared open models and competitive with prominent closed chat systems on helpfulness/safety; safety work reduced unsafe outputs but factuality, reasoning, multilingual breadth and prompt sensitivity remained limitations.
3) ArXiv 2310.06825, `Mistral 7B`; authors Albert Q. Jiang; Alexandre Sablayrolles; Arthur Mensch; Chris Bamford; Devendra Singh Chaplot; Diego de las Casas; Florian Bressand; Gianna Lengyel; Guillaume Lample; Lucile Saulnier; Lélio Renard Lavaud; Marie-Anne Lachaux; Pierre Stock; Teven Le Scao; Thibaut Lavril; Thomas Wang; Timothée Lacroix; William El Sayed; published 2023-10-10. Method: 7B decoder-only architecture combining GQA and SWA with rolling KV cache and chunked prefill; plus instruction-fine-tuned version. Results: outperformed Llama 2 13B across reported benchmark groupings and Llama 1 34B on many reasoning, math, code tasks; competitive with CodeLlama 7B while stronger generally; instruct variant beat compared 7B instruction models; reduced attention-cache and inference costs.

Acceptance: file exists at exact path, begins with required heading + intro, contains all author names and method/results for all three papers, and validation confirms structure.
Build Word paper synthesis

Create a Google Spreadsheet titled exactly `LLM Paper Registry`. In its primary sheet, write exactly these six columns in this order: ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Key_Contribution, Method_Category. Add one row for each of the three included papers below; do not add the excluded robotics paper. Preserve author names in one semicolon-separated cell. Use ISO dates. Format the header for readability and freeze the top row if supported. Verify by reading back the populated range. Return spreadsheet ID, URL, sheet name, and verification summary.
